key_insight: The paper introduces a discrete diffusion framework that enables direct generation over high-dimensional pretrained representation tokens (e.g., 768–1024 dims), bridging the semantic richness gap between visual token generation and language-style token prediction.
problem_solved: Existing discrete visual generation methods are restricted to low-dimensional latent tokens (8–32 dims), losing semantic fidelity; this work tackles the challenge of performing discrete generation on high-dimensional representation tokens while preserving semantic structure.
method: Define a discrete diffusion process operating on high-dimensional representation tokens, tailored to preserve semantic relationships in pretrained feature spaces.
Design training and sampling procedures that handle the combinatorial complexity of large token dimensions without collapsing semantic content.
Leverage pretrained high-dimensional encoders as token spaces so generated outputs maintain richer semantics and are compatible with language-style token prediction.
impact: Enables unified, token-based visual generation that retains semantic richness from high-dimensional representations, simplifying integration with multimodal and language-model-style architectures and improving downstream understanding and synthesis.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: low-dimensional token pipeline vs. high-dimensional representation-token pipeline to show semantic gap
Schematic of the cubic discrete diffusion process (forward corruption and reverse denoising over discrete high-dim tokens)
Embedding-space visualization (t-SNE/UMAP) showing preservation of semantic clusters before and after generation
Qualitative comparison grid of generated samples from low-dim baselines and the proposed method to highlight fidelity improvements
paper_title: Cubic Discrete Diffusion: Discrete Visual Generation on High-Dimensional Representation Tokens
paper_authors: Yuqing Wang, Chuofan Ma, Zhijie Lin, Yao Teng, Lijun Yu
